The Umananda Temple stands on Umananda (Peacock) Island, said to be the smallest inhabited riverine island in the world, in the middle of the Brahmaputra off Guwahati. It sits atop the rocky hill of Bhasmachala (Bhasmakuta - 'hill of ashes'): per the Kalika Purana, when Kamadeva disturbed Shiva's meditation here, Shiva opened his third eye and burned him to ashes; Shiva is also said to have resided here as Bhayananda and imparted knowledge to Parvati. The temple was built in 1694 CE by Bar Phukan Garhganya Handique on the orders of the devout Shaivaite Ahom King Gadadhar Singha; the original brick structure was badly damaged in the 1897 Assam earthquake and rebuilt by a wealthy local merchant, with restoration work including some Vaishnavite inscriptions inside. Noted for its rock-cut figures and sculptures by Assamese craftsmen, and home to golden langurs on the island. Reachable only by ferry/boat from Kachari Ghat, Uzanbazar or Sukleshwar Ghat (10-15 min ride), then a steep climb of ~100-230 steps.

town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Northeast India, spread along the south bank of the Brahmaputra river in Kamrup Metropolitan district; Dispur, the capital of Assam, is its eastern suburb. Known as the 'City of Temples', it hosts Kamakhya, Umananda, Navagraha, Sukreswar and other historic shrines, plus the IIT Guwahati campus across the river. It is the gateway to the Northeast, well connected by air, rail and road.
